name: Accenture
seo_title: Accenture case interview and assessments: what to expect
description: What Accenture's own careers pages say about its online assessment, interviews and case study interviews, each line linked to its source.
intro: This guide sums up what Accenture's own careers pages say about applying and interviewing, from how to apply to what Accenture looks for and how to prepare. It reflects those pages as we checked them on 16 October 2026. Processes differ by programme, role and country, so check Accenture's careers site for your role before you apply.

items.text: Accenture says its UK Strategy & Consulting graduate programmes have four pathways: Consulting, Strategy, Digital Engineering & Manufacturing (Industry X), and AI & Data.

For its UK Consulting and Strategy graduate programmes, Accenture says it welcomes applicants from any degree subject, but they need a bachelor's degree, or to be on track for one, by their start date.
Accenture says its UK graduate programmes have no minimum degree classification, although some programmes require a particular degree subject.
Accenture says UK early-careers applications must be made through its website, and speculative applications sent any other way, such as a CV or cover letter, are not considered.
Accenture says its UK programmes recruit on a rolling basis and close once it has enough applications rather than on a set date, so it recommends applying early.

Accenture asks UK early-careers candidates to apply to only one programme and one location at a time, and says unsuccessful candidates must wait six months before reapplying to any Accenture programme.

Accenture says every UK early-careers candidate who passes the application stage, whatever the programme, is invited to the Accenture Discovery Portal, an online assessment made for Accenture that looks at key skills and strengths.
Accenture says the Discovery Portal is not timed and it expects it to take about 60 to 90 minutes; the time is recorded but does not count towards the result, and candidates cannot prepare for it.
Accenture says it cannot give individual feedback at the UK application stage, but every candidate who completes its online assessment receives a personalised feedback report.

Accenture says UK candidates who pass the online assessment are invited to a Task Based Interview: an online interview in which they discuss with a recruiter how they would respond to work-based scenarios.
Accenture says the next UK stage is an in-person Business Strengths Interview with a Manager or Managing Director, which uses a strengths-based approach and lasts about 50 to 60 minutes.
Accenture's careers blog says a behavioural interview looks at how you manage and overcome difficult situations, and suggests answering with the STAR method (Situation, Task, Action, Result).

For its UK Strategy, AI & Data and Digital Engineering, Manufacturing & Supply Chain graduate programmes, Accenture says there is an extra case study interview at the final, face-to-face interview stage.

Accenture's Case Interview Workbook (copyright 2018) says case interviews typically last 45 to 60 minutes, with 30 to 45 minutes on the case itself, and that cases are often drawn from the interviewer's own project experience.

The workbook says success in a case interview does not depend on finding the correct answer, but on how clearly you define the problem, how logically you structure your analysis, your quantitative skills and how well you communicate.
The workbook says the interviewer's case description may be one sentence or a page long, and the interviewer may ask you to do simple analyses to test your hypotheses.
Accenture's case-study interview blog says the focus can vary: the interviewer may spend the first half asking about your previous experience, or may start with the case straight away.
The same blog says you can use pen and paper to sketch out your thinking, and can ask the interviewer to define an acronym or to repeat or confirm details.
Accenture says using AI products during interviews to generate answers for you is not permitted and can lead to disqualification, and that it uses proctoring tools and AI-detection methods.
Accenture says candidates may use AI to rehearse for interviews, but in the interview itself it wants to hear from the candidate, not a script.

For its UK early-careers process, Accenture says it encourages using generative AI, when appropriate, to prepare applications and interviews, but asks for candidates' own authentic participation in most of the assessment process and tells them to follow instructions on when not to use it.

sections.heading: What Accenture looks for and how to prepare

items.text: For its UK Strategy graduate programme, Accenture says it looks for curious, creative and critical thinkers who communicate clearly, with analytical skills, flexibility, resilience and a proactive mindset; Excel, Power BI or Tableau experience helps but is not essential.
Accenture's careers blog says that in behavioural interviews it looks for collaboration, leadership, problem-solving, ability to learn, business acumen and emotional resilience.
Accenture's case workbook says that, beyond the case itself, candidates are also judged on qualities such as poise, communication, flexibility, energy and drive, initiative and managing time.
For its UK Business Strengths Interview, Accenture says it shares detailed preparation guidance beforehand and recommends joining its regular live Q&A sessions for candidates at that stage.

practice_advice: Practise saying your structure out loud before you start any analysis, so the interviewer can follow your plan.
Do short, timed mental maths drills most days, with pen and paper only. Mock Partner's drills cover mental maths, chart reading and market sizing.
After each practice case, write down one thing to do better and choose your next case to work on it.
